proposal.name: Live Coach Studio
proposal.one_liner: A call cockpit, not a chat app: the persona talks, an amber coach rail whispers the next move, a live rubric fills in as the call runs, and every score links back to a transcript line. One shadcn/ui system, with Tremor-style analytics confined to the screens where analytics belong.
proposal.lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the lens on analytics and manager-first thinking: Tremor-style KPI, BarList and Tracker patterns, and a team view that is the richest screen in the app. Changed two things. (1) shadcn/ui is the single system of record, not Tremor plus shadcn. Both are Radix, Tailwind and Recharts underneath, so two kits double the theming surface; Tremor blocks are copied in only where they fit the tokens. (2) Charts stay off the live call, the hardest screen. Analytics live in debrief, progress and team. Research: the Mobbin live-call screens and the Second Nature, Hyperbound and Outdoo pages show scoring that either stops when practice ends or runs only after a real call. None of the pages I read show in-call coaching cues during a practice call.

design_language.typography: Geist for UI and headings (600 weight, -0.02em tracking on display sizes). Geist Mono for timers, scores, timestamps and token counts, with tabular numerals. Body 15px over 1.6 on desktop, 16px on mobile. Scale 12, 14, 16, 20, 28, 40. Inter and Sora are dropped.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 10px radius on controls, 16px on cards, 1px hairlines, no glass or blur. Depth comes from tonal surface steps and a 1px ring. The only glow in the product is the amber coach cue. Focus rings are 2px primary with a 2px offset.
design_language.motion: Coach cue slides up 12px and fades in over 180ms. Rubric bars spring-fill over about 600ms. The orb pulses to audio level and flattens when the persona is silent. Under prefers-reduced-motion everything becomes opacity-only.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75px stroke. One custom mark for the coach: a speech bubble with a spark. No emoji in the app or the README.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default. Dark follows the system through next-themes, and the live call defaults to dark so the orb and cue lane stay legible. Both modes are CSS variables on :root with a dark override. Dark values: canvas #0A0F1C, surface #121A2B, ink #E7ECF5, muted #93A0B8, primary #6B8CFF, coach #FBBF24, ai #A78BFA, on-track #4ADE80, at-risk #FB7185.

proposal.live_coaching_and_scoring: Engine: after each finalised turn, the server sends the last six turns, the rubric and the talk-track state to a coach model (GPT-4.1-mini by default) with structured output: next best question, objection type with its trigger quote, current talk-track step, and rubric deltas, each with an evidence line and a status of provisional or confirmed. Target: a cue visible under 2 seconds after the rep stops speaking. The coach never writes to the persona's channel. v1 cues are visual only, so the persona cannot hear them. Modes: Silent, Light (objections and step changes only), Full. Live scores use the same grader prompt as the debrief, so they differ only in whether a quote is confirmed. If the coach times out, the cue lane shows 'Coach paused' and the call continues. Self-score D: 6.5. Above baseline on the evidence links and the no-leak design; not higher, because live scoring is not yet checked against human raters.
proposal.persona_library_and_wizard: Persona files are YAML in /personas/<job>/<slug>.yaml, validated by the same zod schema the wizard uses, so a contributor's file and an AI draft have identical shape. Launch target: 15 sales jobs (SDR cold call, AE discovery, SaaS, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections), 120 personas in total. Forty are reviewed at v1 and the rest carry a Draft badge. Filters: job, industry, difficulty, call type and objection type. Every persona gets a review checklist for stereotyping, especially in insurance, mortgage and auto. The wizard runs four steps (Source, Draft, Shape, Dry run) and turns a job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or pasted call into a persona, scenario and rubric, with every field traced to its source sentence. Self-score E: 6.0. The generation path is strong; the review load of 120 personas is the real cost.

proposal.openai_fund_angle: OpenAI use is visible and auditable. Each debrief footer reads 'Graded by GPT-4.1-mini, 9 turns, with token count and latency'. An in-app Models page lists which OpenAI model runs grading, coaching, the persona wizard and the optional Realtime voice engine. The README hero carries the text 'Built with OpenAI models' with no logo, pending brand approval. Codex is the contributor path: AGENTS.md at the repo root; a 'Contribute a persona' button opens a prefilled YAML PR template and a Codex CLI prompt; a Codex-powered PR review action checks persona files against the zod schema; release notes are drafted with Codex. These map to the program's named fits: PR review, maintainer automation and release workflows. Apply to the Codex open source fund (grants up to $25,000 in API credits for projects using Codex CLI and OpenAI models) and to Codex for Open Source. The program page excerpt mentions six months of an additional benefit without detail, so confirm terms before applying.

presentation.pitch: Flight Deck Cockpit makes every practice call a flight with one shared visual grammar. Before the call there is a pre-flight briefing: status lamps for mic level, persona loaded and goal read, and Start flight stays locked until mic and goal are green. During the call there is a dark HUD. Six rubric tape gauges move after every rep turn with their weights and tallies, such as Discovery 3 of 10. At most two coach cue cards sit on the right, each with a one-tap Use line. A mono timer and an On course lamp sit in the top bar. After the call there is a black-box debrief. It has a scrubbable timeline with a score curve and event markers, and the gauges rewind as you scrub. Evidence chips seek to the exact second a quote was said. Dark is the default only for flight and debrief. Library, wizard, logbook and team run in a daylight theme, and both themes come from one token file. The library is faceted, the wizard is five steps with confidence chips and a mandatory test flight, and there is a manager 'flight ops' view. The stack is shadcn/ui, Tailwind v4, Motion, Recharts, and Sora, Inter and JetBrains Mono. Against today's chat-bubble live screen, with its orb and a red End button beside the input, this is a different product. The visual identity is the most ownable of my five.
presentation.strongest: Craft and system coherence. Gauges, lamps and mono telemetry are one instrument vocabulary that carries from pre-flight to HUD to debrief to logbook dials. The shape rules are disciplined: hairlines instead of shadows, a 1px inner highlight, and only the live element gets a cyan glow. The type stack is specific, with tabular-nums mono so scores never jitter. The black-box replay, where the gauges rewind as you scrub, is the signature interaction. It makes the debrief the opposite of today's one long scroll. The amber Estimate lamp turns today's silent keyword-fallback F grade into an honest labelled state. The mobile long-press End and grade with a progress ring fixes the exact thumb-zone flaw visible in the current mobile-04 screenshot.
presentation.weakest: Three things. (1) The theme split is a seam. Library and wizard are daylight, then pre-flight and flight are dark. The proposal never says what theme the pre-flight screen uses. If it is daylight, the rep gets a lighting jolt exactly when they should be focusing. The proposal says light is the browsing default and dark is for live and debrief, which is a deliberate choice but a risky one. (2) The metaphor is heavy. Fly, Brief, Black box, Logbook and Flight ops will read as costume to some enterprise buyers, and six gauges plus a cue stack plus a flight-log transcript is a crowded screen for someone mid-sentence. The jurors flagged this. (3) The library is unsized. 'A large open persona set' has no count, and the facet examples omit auto, real estate, retail and recruiting. I also could not verify the stack claims. I tried the Firecrawl lookup for shadcn defaulting to Base UI and Radix status, but it was rate limited, so the 'Base UI became default in July 2026' claim is unconfirmed. The proposal itself flags that its sources disagree on Radix. XL scope, including a Tailwind 3 to 4 migration touching every screen.
presentation.live_coaching_verdict: Above baseline, by a modest margin. A separate grader sidecar runs after each rep turn and returns rubric deltas plus at most one cue, rendered only to the rep, so the persona stays forbidden to coach. Cues come from fixed categories with evidence quotes, and live gauges and the final grade share one rubric, so they cannot silently disagree. Honest fallback via the Estimate lamp. Gaps: no cue-latency target is stated at all, and a one-cue-per-20-seconds throttle can silence a fast call or let a cue land after its moment. It is a per-turn call, not streaming. On screen, the combination of gauges, cues and talk-track ticks is the richest live feedback surface of the five, and it is the one at most risk of overloading the rep.
presentation.persona_library_verdict: About at baseline, slightly above on UX and below on content. The wizard is strong: five steps (Source, Persona, Scenario, Rubric, Test flight), source tabs, streaming fields with confidence chips, rubric weight sliders that total 100, and a save gate behind a test flight. The same zod schema validates wizard output, CI and contributor PRs. Facets cover role, industry, difficulty, objection type and mode, with counts and 'flown N times' social proof. But the seed library is never sized or dated, so a brief that asks for every sales job at open-source level has no number to check against. UI is good, content commitment is vague.

board_reasons: The most coherent design system on the board (gauges, lamps and mono telemetry carry from pre-flight to HUD to black-box replay to logbook), though the dark/daylight theme seam and heavy metaphor are real costs.

proposal.name: Composed Coaching Console
proposal.one_liner: A fixed design system in which the AI composes each call's live coaching and debrief from a closed set of typed blocks, so every layout is personal to the call yet unmistakably on-brand.
proposal.lens_followed_or_changed: Followed: the debrief is composed per call. The grader streams an ordered plan of typed blocks (ScoreHero, MomentReplay, CriterionCard, PatternCallout, DrillCTA), and the coach streams cue blocks during the call. Changed: research showed the AI SDK's streamUI (React Server Components) is marked experimental, so I use AI SDK UI (useChat plus typed tool parts) with a client-side block registry. The model picks blocks and their order from a closed catalogue and never emits markup, which protects brand, accessibility and reliability. Every block must cite transcript turn IDs that validate against the transcript, with a classic fixed-order debrief as fallback. Self-scores (1-10): A 8, B 7, C 8, D 6 (only if cue latency stays under about 1.5 s), E 6, F1 6, F2 5, F3 3 (leans worth building).

design_language.typography: Geist Sans: 600 for display, 400 for body at 16/24 minimum. Geist Mono for timers, scores and timestamps. Debrief grade numeral set at 56/60 in Mono.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Radius 14px cards, 10px controls, 999px chips. Depth from hairlines and tonal surface steps. Live elements get a 1px signal glow ring. No blurred gradient orb.
design_language.motion: Blocks stream in with a 180ms rise and fade. Meters tween over 600ms. Cue cards enter from the rail edge and dismiss after 8s unless pinned. Everything reduces to opacity under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 16 and 20px, stroke 1.75. AI-generated content carries a single spark glyph in signal colour so the rep always knows what the model wrote.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark default for the live console and focus; light for the library, progress and print-friendly debrief. Both via :root tokens with data-theme, following prefers-color-scheme when unset.

proposal.live_coaching_and_scoring: Two streams. The coach runs a small OpenAI-compatible model on each rep turn, debounced, and streams typed cue blocks (whisper, objection alert, next question, talk-track step) plus rubric deltas. Each cue cites the transcript turn it reacts to, and the persona never sees coaching. Coach mode fades scaffolding: Blind shows only the score after the call, Guided adds cues and live meters, Coached adds interrupt-style nudges. Live scores are labelled as estimates. The final grade still comes from the full rubric grader with verbatim quotes. Cap at three cues per minute so the rail never overwhelms the rep, and show a small cost meter for the session.
proposal.persona_library_and_wizard: The library ships as data packs: one JSON or YAML file per persona holding role, seniority, temperament, objections, opening line, voice ID and rubric weights, validated by zod in CI. Target at launch: about 150 personas across the 18 industries in the brief and six job families (SDR cold, AE discovery, CS, support, collections, recruiting). The wizard turns a job description, product URL, CRM note or pasted call into a draft pack, with provenance chips on every field and a rehearsal before save. Its export is the same pack file, so the wizard doubles as a contributor on-ramp for the open-source core.

proposal.openai_fund_angle: Show the models in the UI: a model-slot strip on the landing page, and in every debrief footer the grader model name, rubric version and token cost, so reviewers see efficient use of API credits. implementation.migration_path: Phase 1 (weeks 1-2): Tailwind v4 and shadcn/ui init, token migration, Geist in place of Inter and Sora, rebuilt AppShell, buttons and cards. Phase 2: live call console and block registry behind a feature flag, with the current debrief kept as fallback. Phase 3: debrief composer, then the persona pack loader and library. Phase 4: wizard, landing hero, progress and team views. Scenarios move from localStorage to pack files, with Prisma for org overrides. Existing API routes and the grader contract stay unchanged.

risks: AI-composed layouts can drift or read as inconsistent; mitigate with a closed block registry, a layout grammar and the classic fixed-order fallback.
Live coach latency and token cost; mitigate with a small model, debounced turns, a cue cap and a visible cost meter.
Live scores can look authoritative; label them as estimates and keep the final rubric grade canonical.
Persona quality depends on authoring; mitigate with pack CI, schema validation and a review checklist for contributors.
Copy-in shadcn code adds maintenance; document ownership and pin versions.
Streaming cues can overload screen-reader users; use aria-live polite with throttling and a text transcript path.
Second Nature, Hyperbound and Yoodli already market live coaching; our edge is open, inspectable and forkable, and the team needs to prove it in the demo.

presentation.pitch: Composed Coaching Console is a dark, calm coaching console on one fixed design system (shadcn, Tailwind v4, Geist, hairlines, teal for anything the AI wrote). The twist is that the AI picks which blocks appear for each call, from a closed set of typed blocks (ScoreHero, MomentReplay, CriterionCard, PatternCallout, DrillCTA, plus live cue blocks). It never writes markup, and every block must cite transcript turns that validate, with a classic fixed-order debrief as the fallback. On a live call the rep sees speaker lanes with a small score chip on each of their turns (+3 Discovery), a five-criterion rubric strip that ticks up as they cover ground, a next-best-question chip, talk-track dots, a coral objection bar, and at most two amber whisper cards that quote the exact line that triggered them and fade after 8 seconds. A Blind / Guided / Coached dial stays visible before, during and after the call. The debrief opens on the one turn that cost the deal, then criteria with playable quotes, patterns, and a drill for the weakest skill. The library is about 150 zod-validated persona packs. The wizard takes a job description, URL, CRM note or pasted call, fills a persona card field by field with a source chip on each field, lets the rep tune it by chat ('make them more skeptical'), runs a 60-second rehearsal, then saves or exports the same pack file a contributor would write. For the OpenAI fund it has the cleanest story: a model-slot strip on the landing page, grader model, rubric version and token cost in every debrief footer, a Realtime voice path next to ElevenLabs, and Codex reviewing persona PRs.
presentation.strongest: It is built around how coaches actually develop reps. It opens the debrief on the moment that cost the deal, not a letter grade. It puts a visible dial on how much scaffolding the rep gets (Blind, Guided, Coached), so coaching fades as skill grows. It quotes the trigger line in every cue, and the debrief ends in a drill on the weakest criterion. Every AI claim links to validated transcript turns, which reps and managers can trust. It also has the best fund story of the five: model, rubric version and cost are on screen, and the persona pack file is both the wizard's output and the contributor on-ramp.
presentation.weakest: The generative layout is the least valuable and riskiest part. Reps and managers want the same scorecard shape every time so they can compare calls, and the proposal's own fixed-order fallback admits the composition step can fail. The real coaching value (MomentReplay, DrillCTA, scaffold dial) does not need generative ordering, so I would ship those in a fixed order first and keep composition as an experiment. The D score depends on a sub-1.5-second coach stream that does not exist yet, and the three-cues-per-minute cap makes coaching sparse. Effort is labelled L but stacks a Tailwind v4 migration, AI SDK UI, AI Elements and a block registry, so it is really XL. The family list is only six (SDR cold, AE discovery, CS, support, collections, recruiting), with industry carrying the rest. The dark navy plus teal look is tasteful but close to generic dark-tech. Radix is still supported, but shadcn now defaults to Base UI (I confirmed the July 2026 changelog), so the stack should be pinned deliberately.
presentation.live_coaching_verdict: Exceeds baseline (6.9), conditional on latency. It has every baseline element (whisper cues, next-best question, objection alert, talk-track progress, live rubric). It adds per-turn score chips, cues that quote their trigger line, an Ask coach button and a three-position scaffolding dial. Live numbers are labelled estimates and the full-rubric grader stays canonical. It falls to baseline if cues land later than about 2 seconds, and the 3-cues-per-minute cap is a sensible guard against overload. This is the strongest live-coaching model of my five by a small margin over P02.
presentation.persona_library_verdict: Slightly above baseline (6.4). About 150 packs across 18 industries, filterable by job family, industry, difficulty, objection type and mode, with personal-best rings and a dashed Build your own tile first. The wizard is among the best: a chat-plus-card draft with a source chip per field, tune presets, a 60-second rehearsal and a PR-ready export. Six job families is narrower than the brief's list, and 150 reviewed personas are a content project the UI cannot solve.

board_reasons: The Blind/Guided/Coached dial and trigger-quote cues are real coaching craft and the OpenAI footer (model, rubric version, cost) is a clean fund story, but the look is generic dark navy plus teal and AI-composed layout is the riskiest, least valuable part.

The Blind/Guided/Coached dial is real scaffolding-fade pedagogy and opening the debrief on the turn that cost the deal is how great coaches debrief, but AI-chosen layouts hurt call-to-call comparability, so ship the fixed-order version first.

The strongest OpenAI-model story (typed blocks from structured outputs, model, rubric version and cost in every debrief footer, validated transcript citations) with a fixed-order fallback, though the generative layout is the riskiest part and the true scope is XL, not L.

The visible Blind/Guided/Coached dial and a debrief that opens on the turn that cost the deal are strong learnability ideas, but AI-ordered debrief layouts hurt call-to-call comparability and add a failure mode that the coaching value does not need.

Coach-mode dial, cue quoting and a per-debrief model and cost footer are strong, but AI-composed debrief layouts undercut the same-shape scorecard managers need to compare calls, and L effort really stacks to XL.

why_no: Generative layout is the riskiest bet in the set. A model that chooses the debrief's block order on every call can make two reps' reports look like different products, which hurts the team view and any side-by-side comparison of calls. The closed catalogue and fixed-order fallback only contain the drift without removing it. Every debrief also gains a composition step with its own latency and token cost, and the L effort label hides a lot of new engineering: block registry, grader plan schema, citation validation, AI Elements, and a Tailwind 4 move in weeks 1 to 2.

Per-call composed layouts add a reliability surface that is hard to QA: schema validation, layout drift across an open-ended set of compositions, and reps who expect predictable scoring from a sales tool. Its own live-coaching score of 6 holds only if cue latency stays under about 1.5 seconds, and the three-cues-per-minute cap makes coaching deliberately sparse. The filter rail covers six job families (SDR cold, AE discovery, CS, support, collections, recruiting) with industry carrying the rest, so 'every sales job' is less explicit than in other proposals. The visual language is a tidy dark console rather than a striking look, and an L-sized build stacks a Tailwind v4 migration, AI SDK and AI Elements at once.

The AI-composed layout is the riskiest idea in the set: block sequences can drift and make debriefs read as inconsistent, the sub-1.5-second cue latency it needs is untested, and the launch covers only six job families, short of the brief's 'every sales job' bar.

The generative debrief is the riskiest idea in the council. Layouts that change from call to call are harder to test, harder to make accessible and easier to read as inconsistent, and the proposal's own fallback concedes the point. Its library names six job families and 18 industries, which is thinner than the brief's list of named sales jobs, and its live coaching still depends on a coach stream that does not exist yet.

The model-composed layout is the riskiest idea in the set. Block order can drift, screens will be hard to compare across calls, and the fixed-order fallback is an admission the core can fail. Live coaching is self-scored at 6 and depends on a sub-1.5-second coach stream that is not built yet; cue latency decides the whole live-coaching claim. The look (near-black navy, teal, hairlines) is tasteful but close to the generic dark-tech style that Linear-style competitors already own, so it may not stand out. The 150-persona target across 18 industries is a content project the UI cannot solve, and the provenance chips are only as good as the citation validator behind them.

reasons: Timeline-as-spine with tagged moments and Replay-this-moment is the clearest learning loop and the most accessibility-aware HUD, but the visual language is the least new and the library is the least designed screen.

Timeline as spine, tagged moments, Replay-this-moment retakes and consent labels form the strongest after-call practice loop, but live coaching is only at standard and launch is about 40 hand-checked personas.

A concrete Codex CLI job in CI reviewing persona-pack PRs, one zod schema shared by wizard, importer and CI, and a timeline spine that links every score to a moment make it the best-aimed fund pitch, though the look is the least new and the waveform scrubber needs accessibility work.

A film-room timeline with Replay this moment is the best learning loop and the most accessibility-literate spec (persistent dismissable cue, 44px targets, AA ratios written down), though the 20-second cue gap and an unkeyboardable waveform are real gaps.

verdict.summary:
The composite is a statistical tie: P19 6.90, P39 6.87, P47 6.83, P12 6.78, P26 6.75, a 0.15 spread, and P09 sits 0.01 behind P26 with no seat picks. So I ranked by what the five seats did. P26 is on all five personal lists and first on four. P39 is on all five lists. P19, P47 and P12 are on three each. Borda points (5 for first down to 1 for fifth) are P26 23, P39 15, P19 8, P47 8, P12 6.

The real choice is one axis. P26 is the most executable and fundable plan: the best live-coaching score of all 25 (D 6.94), the best worth-building score (F3 2.92) and measurable cue gates. It also has the weakest look of the five (C 5.52), and it keeps today's blue and ink, which is the brief's own "generic" diagnosis. P39 is the opposite: the highest Look (A 8.48) and second-highest Unique (C 8.78) of all 25, but XL scope, the weakest business case (F1 4.54) and an unsized library. On the A to E mean alone, P39 leads at 7.41 and P26 is last at 6.77, so P26's lead is about delivery risk, not design merit.

My verdict is to build P26's spine in P39's skin. The two dark live-call palettes already have near-identical backgrounds, and the gap is the light-mode primary and the instrument vocabulary, which is a token-level change. P26's discipline (one zod schema, SSRF-safe wizard, latency and precision gates) is hard to retrofit onto P39. If you want one pure proposal, will accept XL scope and want to be remembered, pick P39. Nothing in these five is measured: every latency, precision and persona-count figure is a target.

top5.why_it_won: Copilot Rail Studio. On all five personal lists and first on four. Highest live-coaching score of all 25 (D 6.94) and the lowest not-worth-it score (F3 2.92). The coach is a separate per-turn channel returning schema-checked cues, each citing a transcript turn and a rubric criterion, with an 8-second cooldown and a Use line action that never auto-sends. The persona never sees a cue. It sets measurable gates: p50 cue latency near 2 seconds and cue precision on 30 scripted calls. One zod schema covers wizard, coach and grader. URL import has SSRF protection. A heuristic grade is labelled with a re-grade action. The Models page accepts any OpenAI-compatible base URL. Its own plan says to ship phases 1 to 3 for the fund application and let the team view slip.
top5.biggest_risk: The look. Lowest Unique score of the five (C 5.52), light by default with today's #1D4ED8 blue and #071827 ink, and a side rail beside a transcript is the Gong/Balto pattern. It can read as the generic Tailwind SaaS the brief diagnoses, and its visuals were designed from competitor write-ups rather than live-coaching screenshots, so they are untested. Also: Phase 1 is labelled S but covers the Tailwind v4 move, shadcn and a mobile fix; a 360px rail squeezes the transcript at 1280px; Use line is unclear in voice mode; 200+ personas need a review process.
top5.borrow_from_runners_up: From P39: the daylight surfaces, teal primary and instrument glyphs (the dark stage is already nearly identical), trimmed to three gauges. From P47: the Blind/Guided/Coached dial in place of Whisper/Text only/Off. From P19: hatched-to-solid rubric fills for the Live estimate strip and the AI-versus-manager calibration chart for the team view. From P12: click-to-seek evidence on the debrief moment strip.
top5.best_for: An owner whose deadline is the fund application and who wants the most credible runnable demo, a contributor-ready repo and measurable quality gates, and who will commit to a design pass on the look.

top5.why_it_won: Flight Deck Cockpit. On all five lists, first on my list and second on the UX lead's. Highest Look of all 25 (A 8.48) and second-highest Unique (C 8.78), and the only top-five proposal that answers the brief's generic diagnosis head-on. Pre-flight, HUD, black-box replay and logbook share one instrument grammar. Gauges rewind as you scrub, evidence chips seek to the exact second, an amber Estimate lamp labels fallback grades, and the mobile long-press End and grade fixes the thumb-zone problem in today's mobile capture. Per-flight model and cost readouts suit the fund story.
top5.biggest_risk: Cost and cohesion. XL scope with a Tailwind 3 to 4 migration that touches every screen, the weakest business case of the five (F1 4.54), and a library that is never sized and omits auto, real estate, retail and recruiting from its facets (E 5.78). Six gauges plus two cues plus a flight-log transcript is dense for someone mid-sentence. The dark flight and daylight browse themes meet at a seam, and the flight vocabulary is a learning tax for managers and enterprise buyers. Its claim that shadcn now defaults to Base UI was not verified by its own presenter.
top5.borrow_from_runners_up: From P26: the coach engine spec, acceptance gates, SSRF-safe wizard and Models page; P39 states no cue-latency target at all. From P19: the AI-versus-manager calibration chart, and plain-word labels on manager screens while keeping the flight vocabulary on the rep side. From P12: the accessibility rules (cues that persist until dismissed, 44px targets, a keyboard-operable scrubber with a text alternative).
top5.best_for: An owner who values a memorable first impression and an ownable README GIF over time-to-demo, accepts XL effort, and will cut the HUD to about three gauges.

top5.why_it_won: Live Coach Studio. Top composite (6.90) on the best UX and business scores of the five (B 8.0, F1 6.0, F2 7.14), on three lists. The only proposal with an AI-versus-manager calibration chart, which is what makes a sales leader trust the grader. Hatched-to-solid rubric fills mark provisional versus quote-confirmed scores without relying on colour, charts stay off the live call, and the 15 job tabs match the brief nearly word for word. The most buildable migration: routes kept, Tailwind 3.4 stays in phase 1, and a token-first first week. Fund detail includes AGENTS.md, a Codex PR-review action, model, token and latency in each debrief footer, and Built with OpenAI models as text with no logo pending brand approval.
top5.biggest_risk: It looks like a default template, which it admits. Lowest Look of the five (A 6.98), Unique 5.96, blue #2B50E0 on cool grey, shadcn plus Tremor, and an analytics-first stance that can make a practice room feel like a BI tool. 80 of the 120 launch personas ship as drafts, and the stereotype review checklist for insurance, mortgage and auto is promised, not resourced. Live scoring is not validated against human raters.
top5.borrow_from_runners_up: From P39 or P47: a dark identity and a non-blue primary, so the app stops reading as stock shadcn. From P26: the coach acceptance gates, SSRF-safe URL fetching and cue schema. From P12: the click-to-seek timeline and Replay this moment on the debrief ticks.
top5.best_for: An owner aiming at training firms and call centres who wants managers to trust the grader and the lowest-risk migration, and accepts a plainer look that needs its own design pass.

top5.why_it_won: Composed Coaching Console. The strongest coaching pedagogy and best OpenAI showcase, on three lists. A visible Blind/Guided/Coached dial lets scaffolding fade as the rep improves. The debrief opens on the turn that cost the deal and ends in a drill on the weakest criterion, and cues quote the line that triggered them. Typed blocks come from structured outputs, every block must cite validated transcript turn IDs, and each debrief footer shows grader model, rubric version and token cost. Second-best live-coaching score of all 25 (D 6.88) with strong Look and Unique (A 7.6, C 8.1). It also avoided the experimental streamUI route in favour of AI SDK UI.
top5.biggest_risk: The AI-composed layout is the riskiest and least valuable part. It breaks the same-shape scorecard managers use to compare calls and adds a failure mode (hence its own fixed-order fallback), and the coaching value does not need it. Labelled L but it stacks a Tailwind v4 migration, AI SDK UI, AI Elements and a block registry, so it is really XL. Lowest UX score of the five (B 7.14), weak sell-to-entities score (F2 5.44), only six job families, a sub-1.5 second coach stream that does not exist yet, and a generic dark-navy-plus-teal look.
top5.borrow_from_runners_up: From P26: the cue schema, cooldown and acceptance gates. From P12: the timeline strip as the MomentReplay block. From P19: the AI-versus-manager calibration chart so AI claims get human checks. Ship the typed blocks in a fixed order first and keep composition as a flagged experiment.
top5.best_for: An owner who wants an AI-native story for fund reviewers and cares most about whether reps actually improve, and who will ship the fixed-order version first.

top5.why_it_won: Film Room Sideline. On three lists. The best learning loop: one timeline spine across live call, debrief and progress, with tagged moments, coach and manager annotations, and Replay this moment, which starts a retake from that timestamp. The most accessibility-literate spec (cues persist until dismissed, Esc to dismiss, 44px targets, AA contrast ratios written into the palette). It also has consent and visibility labels on manager views, PII stripped before any model call, and the right engineering order: a measured harness over recorded calls before UI polish. It has the most concrete Codex story, with Codex CLI in CI reviewing persona-pack PRs for schema, bias and rubric weights, plus release-note automation. L effort.
top5.biggest_risk: Lowest live-coaching score of the five (D 6.02) and E 5.76. The 20-second minimum cue gap can hold back help just as an objection lands. The HUD packs a timeline, tag pills, six meters, a checklist and a cue onto one screen. A waveform scrubber is not keyboard or screen-reader accessible by default and implies retained audio, which needs consent and storage rules. It has the least new look (Sora and Inter kept, and Hudl density can read sports-coded), the library is its least designed screen, and only about 40 of the 150+ personas are hand-checked at launch.
top5.borrow_from_runners_up: From P26: the cue schema and a shorter cooldown (8 seconds), with objection alerts exempt from any gap. From P39 or P47: a stronger visual identity, since this look is the least new. From P47: the Blind/Guided/Coached dial. From P19: the calibration chart.
top5.best_for: An owner who wants a calm, light-first, accessibility-literate product built around deliberate practice, with a natural path from practice calls to real-call coaching.

verdict.dissent:
1) Composite versus seats. P19 leads the composite but no seat ranked it first, while P26 is third on composite and first on four lists. With a 0.15 spread I treated the composite as a tie. Three of its eight terms are business viability, which matters less for a fund application than for a startup. On the A to E mean alone P39 leads (7.41) and P26 is last (6.77).
2) P44 Practice Graph Studio deserves a second look. It ties P19 and P47 on seat points (8) and beats P12 (6), and the OSS maintainer ranked it second. Its composite (6.64) kept it out. I would swap it in for P12 if you weight the contributor flywheel over the replay timeline.
3) P09 Live Ledger is 0.01 below P26 on composite, but no seat listed it, so the cutoff stands.
4) Seat splits on P39. I ranked it first and the OSS maintainer ranked it fifth. The UX and enablement seats both want the HUD trimmed. I am also the only seat that picked P23 and P22, so weigh my taste for a bolder or more editorial look accordingly.
5) The Base UI claim is contested. P47's presenter says it confirmed the July 2026 shadcn changelog. P39's presenter could not verify it and notes that sources disagree on Radix. Check it when you run shadcn init and pin the primitive explicitly.
6) This verdict rests on the proposals and presentations as submitted. No cue-latency, precision or persona-count figure in any of them has been measured.
verdict.fund_recommendation:
No UI choice earns the grant. Reviewers read the repo, the README, the demo and how OpenAI models and Codex are used. Do these whichever proposal you pick, roughly in this order.
1) Make Codex use real before you apply. Add AGENTS.md at the repo root, keep Codex CLI visible in the commit and PR history, and add a CI check that validates persona and scenario files against the zod schema with a Codex review comment. Have Codex draft the release notes. Claim only what is true.
2) Make OpenAI use real. Keep the OpenAI-compatible default (gpt-4.1-mini today) for grading, coaching and the persona wizard, using structured outputs. Ship OpenAI Realtime as a working voice engine beside ElevenLabs, and do not mention it in the README until it runs. Show model, latency, tokens and cost in each debrief footer and on a Models page, read from config rather than hard-coded. Use Built with OpenAI models as plain text, with no logo unless brand approval exists.
3) Measure the coach before polishing screens. Run a harness over recorded or scripted calls, target p50 cue latency under about 2 seconds, report cue precision, and publish the numbers in the README.
4) Write a short credit-spend plan: expected tokens per session across grading, per-turn coaching, wizard runs and Realtime voice, with a per-call budget cap.
5) Ship an honest library. Aim for about 40 reviewed personas across the brief's sales jobs, label the rest Draft, and add a stereotyping review checklist for insurance, mortgage, auto and collections. Do not advertise 150 or 200 until they are reviewed.
6) Cover what a reviewer checks in five minutes: a README hero clip of a coached call, one-command self-host, a demo that works in text mode without sign-in, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY.md, issue templates, good-first-issue labels by job family, and persona-file CI.
7) Close the safety questions: recording-consent gating before voice goes live, PII stripping on pasted calls, an SSRF allowlist on URL import, and visual-only cues so the persona never hears the coach.
8) Do the Tailwind 3 to 4 migration as its own PR so the redesign diff stays reviewable.
9) Verify current terms on the official pages before applying; one board note says the program page mentions an extra six-month benefit without detail. Apply to both the Codex open source fund and Codex for Open Source. Apply once the Codex workflow, the Realtime path and the coached live call are demoable. The board's cited sources say the fund is reviewed on an ongoing basis, so the full redesign does not need to be shipped first.
Nothing here guarantees acceptance.
verdict.overlap_warning:
There are two near-duplicate pairs and one shared skin. P39 and P12 have essentially the same debrief: a scrubbable timeline with tagged moments and click-to-seek evidence chips. They sit on near-identical stacks (shadcn, Tailwind v4, Motion, wavesurfer.js, TanStack Table, Recharts, cmdk, and the same Sora, Inter and JetBrains Mono type). They differ in metaphor and tone, cockpit versus film room, not in mechanics, so do not count them as two options. P19 and P26 share the same live-call model: a coach rail with cue cards, a live rubric meter and a talk-track stepper, on shadcn and Geist, light by default with a dark call stage. P47 is close to P26 in its coach channel and differs mainly in the AI-composed debrief. Underneath, all five use dark navy with teal or amber on the call screen, so the real choice is the interaction model, not the look.

The most distinct runner-up is P44 Practice Graph Studio (composite 6.64, three seat picks, Borda tied with P19 and P47). It offers personas as schema-checked files with Edit-as-PR and a Codex review step, a GitHub-style practice graph, and the clearest free-core versus paid-team model. It trades away live coaching and library depth (D 6.0, E 5.38). For a purely visual break, P22 Editorial Ledger (light Swiss editorial) and P23 Switchboard Console (phosphor terminal) are the alternatives, but only my seat picked them.
